In that instant, something became clear.
...Not copies. I had been calling them the wrong thing.

Fragments.

Hikaru—the Silver Star—had torn off pieces of herself, brought these beings into existence, and given them names.

Of course they were so close to the original, then.

Just as strong. Just as sharp. Just as FAST!

en.html:
...Eight elite warriors in front, supporting fire from behind. I doubted they were coordinating on purpose. No matter. By accident or otherwise, it was tactically sound.

A small force can beat a large one through superior tactics. Equal tactics will not do, bhai. At that point the numbers start making the decisions.

They would close around us and crush us.

My duty still unfinished.

Not even having reached the one I was supposed to fight.

　戦術において優ればこそ、寡兵が大軍を打ち負かす

From another direction, a group of copies had been taking aim at us. Now they were falling.
One warrior was tearing through them, sweeping them aside, clearing them out.

Deep-indigo armor. At one glance, an old and famous tsurugi—you could not mistake it.

That was... yes. I had seen it once before.

I had been contaminated at the time, but that memory had stayed. At Kenchouji, Ichijou had armored up into that very form.

She had come also.

Deep-indigo armor. At one glance, an old and famous tsurugi—you could not mistake it.

That was... yes. I had seen it once before.

I had been contaminated at the time, but that memory had stayed. At Kenchouji, Ichijou had armored up into that very form.

She had come also.

en.html:
I knew.
The copy regiment was a threat, but we had some idea of what kind of threat, and how great. That completely unknown 'god' would probably be more dangerous.

That was what I thought.

Also, Ichijou Ayane and Captain Kanae Ootori would surely find it laughable: me, at this late stage, appointing myself their guardian and worrying over their safety. Presumptuous fellow. Who had asked me?

That too was what I thought.

...But understanding the logic did not make everything else agree with it.

I would be abandoning these two. That fact...

　そう思う。

　また、綾弥一条と大鳥香奈枝大尉、この二人にして
みれば今さら俺などに保護者よろしく身を案じられる
など笑止であろう。
　実際、烏滸がましい事に違いない。

　そうも思う。

　……だが。
　理屈では納得できても、理屈を超えた部分では――

　この二人を、見捨てる、という事実が……

en.html:
After those few bare words of parting, we looked away from each other. Each turned to face the battlefield in their own way.

Ichijou Ayane. Kanae Ootori.
...I was leaving them here.

However I looked at it, the difference in strength was hopeless. Against the copy regiment, their chances of survival were probably close to zero.

Knowing that, I would go. Leave them behind.

...Now was not the time to start hesitating.

I had already abandoned people. How many. How many.

A child, only a little while ago. I had left that child to die.

Because I believed the decision was necessary.

—For that very reason.
I would leave these two now also.

I had to.

ja.html:
味も素っ気もない一言だけの挨拶を最後に、俺達は
互いから視線を外した。
　三者三様、戦場に向き合う。

　綾弥一条。大鳥香奈枝。
　……俺は二人をこの場に残す。

　複製連隊との戦力差は、どう考えても絶望的だ。
　二人が生き残る確率は、零に近いだろう。

　それを承知の上で、行く。
　二人を見捨てる。

　……迷うべきではない。

　俺は既に見捨てているのだ。
　幾人も。幾人も。

　先刻も、一人の子供を見捨てて死なせた。

　その決断が必要なのだと信じて。

　――<ruby>だから<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>。
　今も、見捨てる。

　見捨てなければ。
